chapter: Second European tour and the crash
title: Staying in Europe, the crash and the lawyer Hare's warning
summary: Planning to settle in Europe with about $25,000, he joins a Russian and a Frenchman in a business despite the American lawyer's warning.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now. Okay, so you stayed, this time you stayed in Europe for many years, didn't you.
Oh yes. I tell you this time, I was thinking about making it my home.
Thinking very seriously. I had some money. And this was the time, you know, that we had the crash here.

Not having had enough education, I had dropped out in the second year of high school. So in those days, I didn't understand what it meant. This crash really meant. And that if a crash came in a principal country, then it would be felt around the world. I didn't understand that. Well,
in Paris I had, oh I guess I might have been worth about $25,000., you know what I mean, in money.

So what I did was, I met a Russian that had a formula for making waterproofing. Then a Frenchman that had the prestige, being a Frenchman, he could establish anything in France that he wanted. Well, with the three of us, we went into a business. Now, before we went into this business, I want to show you something. What a lot of times the thoughts of prejudice is in your own mind when other people are not thinking about it. So, but I took one of the fellows' advice, and I went to the embassy and I asked for a lawyer. I was going to check on it. They gave me a lawyer, and if he's living, or if any of his people are living, his name was Hare, H-a-r-e. Anyhow, Mr. Hare was from the southlands, and he brought everything to Paris from the southlands that he could, the brogue --

Yeah, he was an American. And so he brought the speech and everything. And so he set up there and he said, 'Well now look here, Mr. Wooding, if I were you all I wouldn't fool with that thing, you know. Because things is not so good now, and we shouldn't do that.' [PAUSE IN TAPE]
